title: Frobenius skew modules, primitive functions and representing data
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] of prime characteristic $p$, and let $A=k_\sigma[F]$, where $\sigma(c)=c^p$. Concretely its additive group is the finite coefficient sequences $\sum c_iF^i$, and $(cF^i)(bF^j)=c b^{p^i}F^{i+j}$; this specializes the skew-polynomial construction. On a commutative $k$-algebra $R$, the formula $(\sum c_iF^i)x=\sum c_i x^{p^i}$ uniquely specifies a left module structure (module terminology as in [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], algebra homomorphisms as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]); no nonzero-ring condition is imposed on $R$. Let $G$ be a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Its $R$-points are $\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}R,G)$, using [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The additive group $\mathbf G_a$ of [def-sc-gm-ga] is commutative. Put $P(G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-groups}}(G,\mathbf G_a)$ with pointwise addition. For $f\in P(G)$ and $g\in G(R)$, write $f_R(g)$ for the value of the composite $\operatorname{Spec}R\to G\to\mathbf G_a=\operatorname{Spec}k[y]$ on $y$. There is a unique left $A$-module structure on $P(G)$ characterized by $((\sum c_iF^i)f)_R(g)=\sum c_i f_R(g)^{p^i}$ for every $R,g$. For a left $A$-module $M$, a representation of $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,-)$ consists of a commutative $k$-group scheme $U$, and additive bijections $\theta_R:U(R)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,R)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, satisfying $\theta_S(U(\phi)(g))(m)=\phi(\theta_R(g)(m))$ for every $k$-algebra map $\phi:R\to S$, $g\in U(R)$, and $m\in M$. No representer is selected by this definition.
